q:

q:

q: A father is currently 3 times as old as his son. 12 years ago, the father was 6 times as old as his son was then. What is the present age of the father?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Let the present age of the son be $x$ years. Then the present age of the father is $3x$.

12 years ago:

  • Son's age $= x - 12$
  • Father's age $= 3x - 12$

According to the given condition: $3x - 12 = 6(x - 12)$

$$\Rightarrow 3x - 12 = 6x - 72$$

$$\Rightarrow 3x = 60 \implies x = 20$$

Present age of the father $= 3x = 3 \times 20 = 60$ years.

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q: What is the remainder when $2^{100}$ is divided by 7?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

We evaluate powers of 2 modulo 7:

  • $2^1 \equiv 2 \pmod 7$
  • $2^2 \equiv 4 \pmod 7$
  • $2^3 = 8 \equiv 1 \pmod 7$

Since $2^3 \equiv 1 \pmod 7$, we can express the exponent $100$ as $3 \times 33 + 1$:

$$2^{100} = (2^3)^{33} \times 2^1 \equiv (1)^{33} \times 2 \equiv 2 \pmod 7$$

Therefore, the remainder is 2.

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: If 'EARTH' is coded as 'GCTVJ' in a certain code language, how will 'GLOBE' be coded in that same language?
ex:
{{

Pattern Analysis:

Each letter is shifted forward by $+2$ positions in the English alphabet:

  • $E (+2) \rightarrow G$
  • $A (+2) \rightarrow C$
  • $R (+2) \rightarrow T$
  • $T (+2) \rightarrow V$
  • $H (+2) \rightarrow J$

Applying the same $+2$ shift to 'GLOBE':

  • $G (+2) \rightarrow I$
  • $L (+2) \rightarrow N$
  • $O (+2) \rightarrow Q$
  • $B (+2) \rightarrow D$
  • $E (+2) \rightarrow G$

Result: INQDG.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q:

While synthetic fertilizers provide immediate short-term yield gains, continuous excessive chemical application without organic matter replenishment destroys microbial communities, accelerates soil acidification, and locks farmers into a cycle of diminishing returns.

Which of the following is the most logical and rational corollary to the passage?
options: Synthetic fertilizers should be immediately prohibited across all agricultural sectors.
Long-term soil fertility necessitates integrating organic matter management alongside balanced nutrient replenishment.
Soil degradation is solely caused by climatic shifts and cannot be mitigated by farm-level interventions.
Chemical inputs improve soil microbial ecosystems if applied at double the recommended dosage.
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 2: The passage shows that reliance on synthetic inputs alone depletes soil organic matter and damages microbial health; thus, sustained soil conservation requires replenishing organic matter and maintaining biological balance.

}}

q: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 minutes and 15 minutes respectively. An outlet pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 minutes. If all three pipes are opened together, in how many minutes will the empty tank be completely filled?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Let total capacity of the tank be $\text{LCM}(12, 15, 20) = 60\text{ units}$.

  • Efficiency of Pipe A $= \frac{60}{12} = +5\text{ units/min}$
  • Efficiency of Pipe B $= \frac{60}{15} = +4\text{ units/min}$
  • Efficiency of Pipe C $= \frac{60}{20} = -3\text{ units/min}$

Combined Net Work per minute $= 5 + 4 - 3 = 6\text{ units/min}$.

$$\text{Time required} = \frac{60}{6} = 10\text{ minutes}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: A person walks 10 meters North, turns right and walks 15 meters, then turns right again and walks 10 meters, and finally turns left and walks 5 meters. How far and in which direction is the person from the starting point?
ex:
{{

Step-by-step Movement:

  • Starting at $(0, 0)$.
  • 10 m North $\rightarrow (0, 10)$
  • Turn right, 15 m East $\rightarrow (15, 10)$
  • Turn right, 10 m South $\rightarrow (15, 0)$
  • Turn left, 5 m East $\rightarrow (20, 0)$

Distance from $(0, 0)$ to $(20, 0) = 20\text{ meters}$ directly towards the East.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: In an examination, 70% of candidates passed in English, 65% passed in Mathematics, and 25% failed in both subjects. If 360 candidates passed in both subjects, what was the total number of candidates who appeared in the examination?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Let total candidates be $100\%$.

  • Failed in English $= 100 - 70 = 30\%$
  • Failed in Mathematics $= 100 - 65 = 35\%$
  • Failed in both $= 25\%$

Percentage failing in at least one subject $= 30 + 35 - 25 = 40\%$.

Percentage passing in both subjects $= 100\% - 40\% = 60\%$.

Given: $60\% \text{ of Total} = 360$

$$\text{Total Candidates} = \frac{360 \times 100}{60} = 600$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E, and F are sitting in a circle facing the center.
- B is between D and C.
- A is second to the left of E and second to the right of C.
Who is facing D directly across the circle?
ex:
{{

Deduction:

Let the 6 clockwise circular positions be $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$.

  • Place C at position 1.
  • Since A is 2nd to the right of C $\rightarrow$ A is at position 5 (counter-clockwise/right).
  • A is 2nd to the left of E $\rightarrow$ E is at position 3.
  • B is between D and C $\rightarrow$ B is at position 6 and D is at position 5 (or D at 4).
  • Arranging around the circle: Opposite pairs are $(1, 4), (2, 5), (3, 6)$.
  • D is placed at position 6/opposite to E. Hence, E is directly opposite to D.

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the series?
$$3,\; 8,\; 18,\; 38,\; 78,\; ?$$
ex:
{{

Pattern:

Each term is generated by multiplying the preceding number by 2 and adding 2:

  • $3 \times 2 + 2 = 8$
  • $8 \times 2 + 2 = 18$
  • $18 \times 2 + 2 = 38$
  • $38 \times 2 + 2 = 78$
  • $78 \times 2 + 2 = 156 + 2 = \mathbf{158}$

Alternatively, the differences double each time: $5, 10, 20, 40, 80 \implies 78 + 80 = 158$.

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q: A sum of money invested at simple interest triples itself in 10 years. In how many years will it become 7 times the original principal at the same annual rate of interest?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Let the principal be $P$.

When the sum triples, Amount $= 3P \implies \text{Simple Interest (SI)} = 2P$.

$$\text{SI} = \frac{P \times R \times T}{100} \implies 2P = \frac{P \times R \times 10}{100} \implies R = 20\%\text{ per annum}$$

To become 7 times the principal, Amount $= 7P \implies \text{Required SI} = 6P$.

$$6P = \frac{P \times 20 \times T_2}{100} \implies 6 = \frac{T_2}{5} \implies T_2 = 30\text{ years}$$

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q: A train 150 meters long passes a telegraph pole in 10 seconds. How long will it take to cross a platform 250 meters long running at the same speed?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Speed of the train $= \frac{\text{Length of train}}{\text{Time taken}} = \frac{150\text{ m}}{10\text{ s}} = 15\text{ m/s}$.

Total distance to cross the platform $= \text{Length of train} + \text{Length of platform} = 150 + 250 = 400\text{ meters}$.

$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{400}{15} = \frac{80}{3} = 26.67\text{ seconds}$$

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q:
Consider the following statements and conclusion:
Statements:
1. All books are papers.
2. Some papers are desks.
3. All desks are chairs.

Conclusions:
I. Some chairs are papers.
II. Some desks are books.

Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements?
options: Both Conclusion I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
ex:
{{

Syllogism Analysis:

  • Conclusion I: Some papers are desks + All desks are chairs $\implies$ Some papers are chairs $\implies$ Some chairs are papers. (Valid)
  • Conclusion II: We know All books are papers and Some papers are desks, but there is no direct definite overlap given between books and desks. (Invalid)

Therefore, only Conclusion I logically follows.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: A vessel contains 60 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 2 : 1. How much water must be added to this mixture so that the ratio of milk to water becomes 1 : 2?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Initial volume $= 60\text{ L}$ with Milk : Water $= 2 : 1$.

  • Initial Milk $= \frac{2}{3} \times 60 = 40\text{ litres}$
  • Initial Water $= \frac{1}{3} \times 60 = 20\text{ litres}$

Let $x$ litres of water be added. The quantity of milk remains unchanged at 40 L.

$$\frac{40}{20 + x} = \frac{1}{2}$$

$$\Rightarrow 20 + x = 80 \implies x = 60\text{ litres}$$

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q: How many numbers are there between 100 and 1000 which have 3 in the units place and are completely divisible by 3?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

3-digit numbers end in 3 and have a step difference of 10 ($103, 113, 123, \dots, 993$).

Every third such number is divisible by 3 (since adding 30 preserves both the unit digit 3 and divisibility by 3).

The sequence of numbers is: $123, 153, 183, \dots, 993$.

This is an Arithmetic Progression with first term $a = 123$, common difference $d = 30$, and last term $T_n = 993$:

$$993 = 123 + (n - 1) \times 30$$

$$870 = (n - 1) \times 30 \implies n - 1 = 29 \implies n = 30$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q:
In a family of six persons P, Q, R, S, T, and U:
- There are two married couples.
- Q is a doctor and the mother of T.
- S is grandmother of T and mother of P.
- R is a lawyer and father of P.
- U is the brother of T.
How is P related to U?
ex:
{{

Family Tree Analysis:

  • Generation 1: R (Male, Lawyer) married to S (Female, Grandmother).
  • Generation 2: P (Son of R & S) married to Q (Female, Doctor).
  • Generation 3: T and U (Sons/Daughters of P & Q; U is brother of T).

Since Q is the mother of T and U, and P is married to Q, P is the Father of U.

}}

q: A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at compound interest compounded annually. In how many years will it become 16 times of itself at the same rate of compound interest?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Under compound interest, if a principal becomes $2\times$ in 5 years:

$$A = P(1 + r)^5 = 2P \implies (1 + r)^5 = 2$$

We need the sum to become $16P = 2^4 P$:

$$P(1 + r)^T = 2^4 P \implies (1 + r)^T = ((1 + r)^5)^4 = (1 + r)^{20}$$

$$\Rightarrow T = 5 \times 4 = \mathbf{20\text{ years}}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: What is the remainder when $3^{2024}$ is divided by 5?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

By Euler's Totient theorem (or cycle of powers of 3 mod 5):

  • $3^1 \equiv 3 \pmod 5$
  • $3^2 \equiv 4 \pmod 5$
  • $3^3 \equiv 2 \pmod 5$
  • $3^4 \equiv 1 \pmod 5$

The cyclicity of $3^n \pmod 5$ is 4.

$$2024 = 4 \times 506 \implies 3^{2024} = (3^4)^{506} \equiv (1)^{506} \equiv \mathbf{1} \pmod 5$$

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: In a code language, if 'ORANGE' is written as 'PQBOFH', how is 'BANANA' written in that language?
ex:
{{

Pattern Analysis:

Each letter is replaced by the next letter in the English alphabet ($+1$ shift):

  • $O(+1) \rightarrow P$
  • $R(+1) \rightarrow Q$ (with minor variation) $\rightarrow$ Let us verify: $O+1=P, R-1=Q, A+1=B, N+1=O, G-1=F, E+3=H$ or standard sequential $+1, +1, +1, +1, +1, +1$:
  • $B(+1) \rightarrow C$
  • $A(+1) \rightarrow B$
  • $N(+1) \rightarrow O$
  • $A(+1) \rightarrow B$
  • $N(+1) \rightarrow O$
  • $A(+1) \rightarrow B$

Result: CBOBOB.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q:
Passage:
The transition to a circular economy in plastics requires moving beyond mechanical recycling to upstream source reduction and chemical redesign. Mechanical recycling degrades polymer chains, limiting the number of cycles a plastic item can be reused before ending in a landfill or incinerator. Sustainable closed-loop circularity necessitates designing bio-benign, infinitely depolymerizable polymers that retain their mechanical properties across infinite iterations.

Which one of the following statements best reflects the crux of the passage?
options: Mechanical recycling alone cannot achieve true circularity without chemical innovations and material redesign.

}}

q: A car travels from city A to city B at an average speed of 60 km/h and returns from B to A along the same route at an average speed of 90 km/h. What is the average speed of the car for the entire round trip?
ex:
{{

Formula:

For equal distances, the average speed is the Harmonic Mean:

$$\text{Average Speed} = \frac{2xy}{x + y} = \frac{2 \times 60 \times 90}{60 + 90} = \frac{10800}{150} = \mathbf{72\text{ km/h}}$$

Correct Option is 1.

}}

options: Both Conclusion I and II follow

Therefore, both Conclusion I and II follow.

q: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person replaces one of them who weighs 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

$$\text{Total increase in weight} = 8 \times 2.5\text{ kg} = 20\text{ kg}$$

$$\text{Weight of new person} = \text{Weight of replaced person} + \text{Total increase} = 65 + 20 = \mathbf{85\text{ kg}}$$

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q: A trader gives two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on an item having a marked price of ₹2,500. What is the final selling price of the item?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

$$\text{Price after 1st discount (20\%)} = 2500 \times (1 - 0.20) = 2500 \times 0.80 = ₹2,000$$

$$\text{Final Selling Price after 2nd discount (10\%)} = 2000 \times (1 - 0.10) = 2000 \times 0.90 = \mathbf{₹1,800}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: In how many different ways can 5 boys and 4 girls be seated in a row such that no two girls sit adjacent to each other?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

First, seat the 5 boys: Number of ways $= 5! = 120$.

Arranging 5 boys creates 6 available gaps (including ends):

$$\_ B_1 \_ B_2 \_ B_3 \_ B_4 \_ B_5 \_$$

We choose 4 gaps out of 6 for the girls and arrange them:

$$^6P_4 = 6 \times 5 \times 4 \times 3 = 360$$

$$\text{Total ways} = 120 \times 360 = \mathbf{43,200\text{ ways}}$$

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: Three numbers are in the ratio $\frac{1}{2} : \frac{2}{3} : \frac{3}{4}$. The difference between the greatest and the smallest number is 36. What is the value of the smallest number?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Multiplying each term of the ratio by $\text{LCM}(2, 3, 4) = 12$:

$$\text{Ratio} = \left(12 \times \frac{1}{2}\right) : \left(12 \times \frac{2}{3}\right) : \left(12 \times \frac{3}{4}\right) = 6 : 8 : 9$$

Let the numbers be $6x, 8x, 9x$.

Greatest $= 9x$, Smallest $= 6x$.

$$\text{Difference} = 9x - 6x = 3x = 36 \implies x = 12$$

$$\text{Smallest number} = 6x = 6 \times 12 = \mathbf{72}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q:

options: Peatland re-wetting and conservation should be prioritized as critical nature-based climate strategies.
Peatlands should be cleared to cultivate high-yield cereal crops.

q:
Among five friends A, B, C, D, and E:
- B is taller than E but shorter than A.
- C is the tallest.
- D is shorter than B and taller than E.
Who is the second shortest among them?
ex:
{{

Ordering Analysis:

  • 'C is the tallest' $\implies C$ is at position 1.
  • 'B is taller than E but shorter than A' $\implies A > B > E$.
  • 'D is shorter than B and taller than E' $\implies B > D > E$.

Combining the relations in descending height order:

$$C > A > B > \mathbf{D} > E$$

The shortest is $E$, and the second shortest is D.

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q: Find the least number which when divided by 6, 9, 12, 15, and 18 leaves 2 as remainder in each case.
ex:
{{

Calculation:

$$\text{LCM}(6, 9, 12, 15, 18) = 180$$

$$\text{Required least number} = \text{LCM} + \text{Remainder} = 180 + 2 = \mathbf{182}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: In a group of 100 students, 60 study History, 40 study Geography, and 20 study both subjects. How many students study neither History nor Geography?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

$$n(H \cup G) = n(H) + n(G) - n(H \cap G) = 60 + 40 - 20 = 80$$

$$\text{Students studying neither} = \text{Total} - n(H \cup G) = 100 - 80 = \mathbf{20}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q:
Passage:
The expansion of space debris in low Earth orbit threatens the long-term viability of satellite communications and Earth observation infrastructure. A collision between two satellites generates thousands of uncontrollable fragments, which in turn elevates the likelihood of subsequent collisions—a cascading dynamic known as Kessler syndrome. Active debris removal and binding international norms for post-mission satellite disposal are necessary to preserve orbital pathways.

Which one of the following is the most logical and crucial inference from the passage?
options: Unregulated satellite launches without debris remediation mechanisms threaten the sustainability of orbital space.
Low Earth orbit satellites should be completely replaced by terrestrial fiber cables.
Collisions in space produce no hazardous debris for other operational spacecraft.
International treaties cannot regulate outer space activities.
ex:
{{

Correct Option is 1: The passage highlights how orbital collisions create cascading debris (Kessler syndrome), making active debris removal and disposal norms essential to maintain orbital space.

}}

q: A tap can fill an empty cistern in 8 hours, while a leak at the bottom empties the full cistern in 12 hours. If both the tap and the leak operate simultaneously, in how many hours will the cistern be completely filled?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Let total capacity of the cistern $= \text{LCM}(8, 12) = 24\text{ units}$.

  • Inlet tap rate $= +\frac{24}{8} = +3\text{ units/hour}$
  • Leakage rate $= -\frac{24}{12} = -2\text{ units/hour}$

$$\text{Net Rate} = 3 - 2 = 1\text{ unit/hour}$$

$$\text{Time required} = \frac{24}{1} = \mathbf{24\text{ hours}}$$

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q:
Find the missing number in the matrix series:
{{
3425
512169
724?
}}
ex:
{{

Pattern:

Each row represents the square of the hypotenuse ($a^2 + b^2 = c$):

  • Row 1: $3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25$
  • Row 2: $5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169$
  • Row 3: $7^2 + 24^2 = 49 + 576 = \mathbf{625}$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q:
Passage:
The expansion of decentralized renewable mini-grids in rural regions offers an alternative to centralized grid extension. However, their long-term financial viability is frequently threatened when local economic activities fail to generate sufficient productive daytime demand. Which one of the following statements best conveys the central idea of the passage?
options: Decentralized mini-grids must be paired with productive rural load-uses to ensure financial sustainability.

Domestic lighting accounts for the highest electricity revenues in rural areas.

{{

q:
Passage:

q: A can do a piece of work in 10 days, and B can do the same work in 15 days. They work together for 3 days, and then A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the remaining work alone?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Let total work $= \text{LCM}(10, 15) = 30\text{ units}$.

  • Efficiency of A $= \frac{30}{10} = 3\text{ units/day}$
  • Efficiency of B $= \frac{30}{15} = 2\text{ units/day}$

Combined work in 3 days $= 3 \times (3 + 2) = 15\text{ units}$.

Remaining work $= 30 - 15 = 15\text{ units}$.

$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{15}{2} = \mathbf{7.5\text{ days}}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: What is the remainder when $(25^{25} + 25)$ is divided by 26?
ex:
{{

Calculation using Modulo Arithmetic:

$$25 \equiv -1 \pmod{26}$$

$$25^{25} \equiv (-1)^{25} \equiv -1 \pmod{26}$$

Now adding 25:

$$(25^{25} + 25) \equiv -1 + 25 = 24 \pmod{26}$$

Therefore, the remainder is 24.

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q: In a certain code, 'LIGHT' is written as 'MJHIU'. How will 'FLAME' be written in that code?
ex:
{{

Each character is shifted by $+1$ in the alphabet:

  • $L(+1) \rightarrow M$
  • $I(+1) \rightarrow J$
  • $G(+1) \rightarrow H$
  • $H(+1) \rightarrow I$
  • $T(+1) \rightarrow U$

Applying the same $+1$ shift to 'FLAME':

  • $F(+1) \rightarrow G$
  • $L(+1) \rightarrow M$
  • $A(+1) \rightarrow B$
  • $M(+1) \rightarrow N$
  • $E(+1) \rightarrow F$

Result: GMBNF.

Correct Option is 4.

}}

q: A train running at 54 km/h crosses a platform of length 200 meters in 24 seconds. What is the length of the train?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Convert speed to m/s:

$$\text{Speed} = 54 \times \frac{5}{18} = 15\text{ m/s}$$

Total distance covered in 24 seconds:

$$\text{Distance} = 15 \times 24 = 360\text{ meters}$$

$$\text{Total Distance} = \text{Length of train} (L) + \text{Length of platform} (200\text{ m})$$

$$L + 200 = 360 \implies L = 360 - 200 = \mathbf{160\text{ meters}}$$

Correct Option is 3.

}}

q:
Consider the following statements and conclusions:
Statements:
1. All plants are trees.
2. Some trees are shrubs.
3. All shrubs are herbs.

Conclusions:
I. Some herbs are trees.
II. Some plants are shrubs.

Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements?
options: Both Conclusion I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
ex:
{{

Syllogism Analysis:

  • Conclusion I: 'Some trees are shrubs' + 'All shrubs are herbs' $\implies$ 'Some trees are herbs' $\implies$ 'Some herbs are trees'. (Valid)
  • Conclusion II: 'All plants are trees' and 'Some trees are shrubs' does not guarantee an overlap between plants and shrubs. (Invalid)

Therefore, only Conclusion I follows.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: A sum of ₹8,000 invested at compound interest amounts to ₹9,261 in 3 years. What is the annual rate of interest (compounded annually)?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

$$A = P\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)^n$$

$$9261 = 8000\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)^3$$

$$\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)^3 = \frac{9261}{8000} = \left(\frac{21}{20}\right)^3$$

$$1 + \frac{r}{100} = \frac{21}{20} = 1 + \frac{1}{20}$$

$$\frac{r}{100} = \frac{1}{20} \implies r = \frac{100}{20} = \mathbf{5\%}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: A box contains 5 red, 4 white, and 3 black balls. If 3 balls are drawn at random simultaneously, what is the probability that all three balls are of different colors?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Total balls $= 5 + 4 + 3 = 12\text{ balls}$.

Total ways to select 3 balls $= ^{12}C_3 = \frac{12 \times 11 \times 10}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 220$.

Ways to choose 1 Red, 1 White, and 1 Black ball:

$$^5C_1 \times ^4C_1 \times ^3C_1 = 5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60$$

$$\text{Probability} = \frac{60}{220} = \mathbf{\frac{3}{11}}$$

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: If 15% of $A = 20\%$ of $B$, then what is the ratio $A : B$?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

$$0.15 A = 0.20 B$$

$$\frac{A}{B} = \frac{0.20}{0.15} = \frac{20}{15} = \mathbf{\frac{4}{3}}$$

$$A : B = 4 : 3$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: In a family, a man has 4 daughters and each daughter has 2 brothers. How many children does the man have?
ex:
{{

Logical Deduction:

There are 4 daughters. Since each daughter shares the same brothers, there are 2 sons in total.

$$\text{Total children} = 4\text{ daughters} + 2\text{ sons} = \mathbf{6\text{ children}}$$

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: A vendor buys lemons at 6 for ₹10 and sells them at 4 for ₹10. What is his profit percentage?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Cost price (CP) of 1 lemon $= \frac{10}{6} = ₹\frac{5}{3}$

Selling price (SP) of 1 lemon $= \frac{10}{4} = ₹\frac{5}{2}$

$$\text{Profit per lemon} = \frac{5}{2} - \frac{5}{3} = \frac{15 - 10}{6} = ₹\frac{5}{6}$$

$$\text{Profit }\% = \frac{\text{Profit}}{\text{CP}} \times 100 = \frac{5/6}{5/3} \times 100 = \frac{3}{6} \times 100 = \mathbf{50\%}$$

Correct Option is 3.

}}

  • $2^3 = 8$
  • $3^3 = 27$

}}

q: A clock gains 5 seconds every 3 minutes. If it is set right at 7:00 a.m., what time will it show at 7:00 p.m. on the same day?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Total time elapsed from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. $= 12\text{ hours} = 720\text{ minutes}$.

Number of 3-minute intervals $= \frac{720}{3} = 240$.

Total time gained $= 240 \times 5\text{ seconds} = 1,200\text{ seconds}$.

$$\text{Gain in minutes} = \frac{1200}{60} = 20\text{ minutes}$$

Time shown by clock $= 7:00\text{ p.m.} + 20\text{ minutes} = \mathbf{7:20\text{ p.m.}}$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: The perimeter of a rectangular plot is 60 meters and its area is 200 sq. meters. What is the length of its diagonal?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Let length be $l$ and breadth be $b$.

  • Perimeter $= 2(l + b) = 60 \implies l + b = 30$
  • Area $= l \times b = 200$

Using the algebraic identity for the diagonal $d = \sqrt{l^2 + b^2}$:

$$l^2 + b^2 = (l + b)^2 - 2lb = (30)^2 - 2(200) = 900 - 400 = 500$$

$$\text{Diagonal } d = \sqrt{500} = \sqrt{100 \times 5} = \mathbf{10\sqrt{5}\text{ meters}}$$

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: If Monday falls on 1st January of a leap year, what day of the week will 31st December of that same year be?
ex:
{{

Calendar Property:

A non-leap year (365 days) starts and ends on the same day of the week.

A leap year (366 days) has 52 weeks and 2 odd days, meaning the last day of the year (31st December) is 1 day ahead of the first day (1st January).

$$\text{Day on 31st December} = \text{Monday} + 1 = \mathbf{Tuesday}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: A sum of ₹10,000 is invested for 2 years at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually. What is the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on the same sum for the same period at the same rate?
ex:
{{

Formula:

$$\text{Difference} = P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2$$

$$\text{Difference} = 10000 \times \left(\frac{10}{100}\right)^2 = 10000 \times \frac{1}{100} = \mathbf{₹100}$$

q: A number when divided by 899 leaves a remainder of 63. What will be the remainder when the same number is divided by 29?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Let the number be $N = 899k + 63$.

Notice that $899 = 29 \times 31$, which is an exact multiple of 29.

$$\Rightarrow N = (29 \times 31k) + 63 = 29(31k + 2) + 5$$

Therefore, dividing 63 by 29 gives:

$$63 = 29 \times 2 + 5$$

The remainder is 5.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: In a coding system, if 'DOCTOR' is written as 'FQEVQT', how will 'PATIENT' be written in that system?
ex:
{{

Each letter is shifted forward by $+2$ positions in the English alphabet:

  • $D(+2) \rightarrow F$
  • $O(+2) \rightarrow Q$
  • $C(+2) \rightarrow E$
  • $T(+2) \rightarrow V$
  • $O(+2) \rightarrow Q$
  • $R(+2) \rightarrow T$

Applying the $+2$ shift to 'PATIENT':

  • $P(+2) \rightarrow R$
  • $A(+2) \rightarrow C$
  • $T(+2) \rightarrow V$
  • $I(+2) \rightarrow K$
  • $E(+2) \rightarrow G$
  • $N(+2) \rightarrow P$
  • $T(+2) \rightarrow V$

Result: RCVKGPV.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

options: Autonomous vehicles will automatically solve urban gridlock without government policy intervention.

q: A work can be finished by 12 men in 18 days. After they have worked for 6 days, 4 more men join them. How many days will all of them take to finish the remaining work?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Total work $= 12\text{ men} \times 18\text{ days} = 216\text{ man-days}$.

Work done in first 6 days by 12 men $= 12 \times 6 = 72\text{ man-days}$.

Remaining work $= 216 - 72 = 144\text{ man-days}$.

New number of men $= 12 + 4 = 16\text{ men}$.

$$\text{Days required for remaining work} = \frac{144}{16} = \mathbf{9\text{ days}}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

options: Both Conclusion I and II follow

Therefore, only Conclusion I follows.

Correct Option is 1.

q: The population of a town increases by 10% in the first year and decreases by 10% in the second year. If the present population is 99,000, what was the population 2 years ago?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Let the population 2 years ago be $P$.

$$P \times \left(1 + \frac{10}{100}\right) \times \left(1 - \frac{10}{100}\right) = 99000$$

$$P \times (1.1) \times (0.9) = 99000$$

$$P \times 0.99 = 99000 \implies P = \frac{99000}{0.99} = \mathbf{1,00,000}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: How many 3-digit even numbers can be formed using the digits $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$ without repetition?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

To form a 3-digit even number, the units place must be filled by an even digit from $\{2, 4, 6\}$ (3 choices).

After choosing the units digit:

  • Tens place can be filled by any of the remaining 5 digits (5 choices).
  • Hundreds place can be filled by any of the remaining 4 digits (4 choices).

$$\text{Total 3-digit even numbers} = 4 \times 5 \times 3 = \mathbf{60}$$

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: At what time between 4 o'clock and 5 o'clock will the hands of a clock be at right angles (90°) to each other for the first time?
ex:
{{

Formula:

$$\text{Time } M = \frac{2}{11} |30H \pm \theta|$$

For $H = 4$ and $\theta = 90^\circ$ (first occurrence using minus sign):

$$M = \frac{2}{11} |30(4) - 90| = \frac{2}{11} |120 - 90| = \frac{2}{11} \times 30 = \frac{60}{11} = \mathbf{5\frac{5}{11}\text{ minutes}}$$

Thus, the hands are at right angles at $4\text{ hours } 5\frac{5}{11}\text{ minutes}$.

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: The sum of ages of 5 children born at intervals of 3 years each is 50 years. What is the age of the youngest child?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

Let the age of the youngest child be $x$.

The ages of the 5 children are $x, x+3, x+6, x+9, x+12$.

$$x + (x + 3) + (x + 6) + (x + 9) + (x + 12) = 50$$

$$5x + 30 = 50 \implies 5x = 20 \implies x = \mathbf{4\text{ years}}$$

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q:

q: Find the missing number in the sequence: $$4,\; 9,\; 19,\; 39,\; 79,\; ?$$
ex:
{{

Pattern:

Each term is obtained by multiplying by 2 and adding 1 ($2n + 1$):

  • $4 \times 2 + 1 = 9$
  • $9 \times 2 + 1 = 19$
  • $19 \times 2 + 1 = 39$
  • $39 \times 2 + 1 = 79$
  • $79 \times 2 + 1 = 158 + 1 = \mathbf{159}$

Alternatively, the differences double each time: $5, 10, 20, 40, 80 \implies 79 + 80 = 159$.

Correct Option is 2.

}}

q: A man rows a boat 18 km downstream in 3 hours and returns upstream in 6 hours. What is the speed of the river stream?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

  • Downstream speed $v = \frac{18\text{ km}}{3\text{ hrs}} = 6\text{ km/h}$
  • Upstream speed $u = \frac{18\text{ km}}{6\text{ hrs}} = 3\text{ km/h}$

$$\text{Speed of current/stream } y = \frac{v - u}{2} = \frac{6 - 3}{2} = \frac{3}{2} = \mathbf{1.5\text{ km/h}}$$

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: If in a certain code 'CLOUD' is written as 'DMPVE', how will 'STORM' be written in that code?

  • $R(+1) \rightarrow S$ (wait: $O+1=P, R+1=S, M+1=N$):
  • $S(+1) \rightarrow T$
  • $T(+1) \rightarrow U$
  • $O(+1) \rightarrow P$
  • $R(+1) \rightarrow S$

Result: TUPSN.

q: Two cards are drawn at random from a standard well-shuffled pack of 52 cards without replacement. What is the probability that both cards are Aces?
ex:
{{

Calculation:

There are 4 Aces in a deck of 52 cards.

  • Probability of 1st card being an Ace $= \frac{4}{52} = \frac{1}{13}$
  • Probability of 2nd card being an Ace (without replacement) $= \frac{3}{51} = \frac{1}{17}$

$$\text{Combined Probability} = \frac{1}{13} \times \frac{1}{17} = \mathbf{\frac{1}{221}}$$

Correct Option is 1.

}}

q: What is the remainder when $(29^{2024} + 31^{2024})$ is divided by 30?
ex:
{{

Calculation using Modulo Arithmetic:

$$29 \equiv -1 \pmod{30} \implies 29^{2024} \equiv (-1)^{2024} \equiv 1 \pmod{30}$$

$$31 \equiv 1 \pmod{30} \implies 31^{2024} \equiv (1)^{2024} \equiv 1 \pmod{30}$$

Adding the two terms:

$$(29^{2024} + 31^{2024}) \equiv 1 + 1 = \mathbf{2} \pmod{30}$$

Therefore, the remainder is 2.

Correct Option is 3.

}}
